newsitem.title: BRAZIL: US, Mercosur at odds over free trade talks - report.
newsitem.headline: US, Mercosur at odds over free trade talks - report.

text.p: The United States has caught its regional trading partners by surprise by changing its proposal for talks leading to an eventual Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA), Brazil's leading financial daily reported on Wednesday.

Gazeta Mercantil said U.S. negotiators taking part in talks in Rio de Janeiro had proposed discussing all aspects of trade liberalization in one stage, beginning after the 1998 FTAA presidential summit in Santiago, Chile.
"We have consulted widely and realized that a majority want to negotiate everything at the same time," the paper quoted Peter Allgeier, head of the U.S. negotiating team, as saying.
The Rio talks, which began Monday evening and run till Thursday, are intended to prepare for a May 15-16 summit of trade ministers in the Brazilian city of Belo Horizonte.
Officials say they hope to end the Rio de Janeiro talks with the blueprint for a Ministerial Declaration to be signed at Belo Horizonte.
